entries.he: שבעת ימים קודם יוה"כ מפרישין כ"ג. שכל עבודת יוה"כ
entries.en: "Seven days before Yom Kippur they separate the Kohen Gadol" - because the entire Yom Kippur service
entries.reviewerEvidence: En correctly renders the Hebrew fragment 'שבעת ימים קודם יוה"כ מפרישין כ"ג. שכל עבודת יוה"כ' including its mid-sentence ending ('...service') matching the Hebrew's own mid-sentence ending ('...עבודת יוה"כ'); the sentence completes in the next Rashi entry, per the corpus's line-based (not sentence-based) entry convention.

entries.he: אינה כשירה אלא בו כדיליף בהוריות בפרק בתרא
entries.en: is valid only when performed by the appointed High Priest, as derived in Horayot (last chapter, 12b).
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew (with 001's tail 'שכל עבודת יוה"כ') reads 'the entire Yom Kippur service is not valid except through him [the Kohen Gadol], as is derived in Horayot, in the last chapter.' The '(דף יב:)' folio marker physically appears at the start of the NEXT vilna line (entry 003) in the printed Vilna edition, but grammatically it modifies 'בפרק בתרא' (the last chapter) here, not entry 003's own clause ('דכתיב...'). Attaching '(last chapter, 12b)' to this entry's English is therefore a correct rendering of the phrase as it naturally reads, not a fabricated or misplaced citation - Horayot 12b is indeed where the Gemara discusses that the Yom Kippur service requires the anointed/appointed Kohen Gadol. Selected for the batch's deterministic blind-QA sample (positional selection by canonical corpus order among provisionally-VERIFIED entries, not risk-based); independently re-reviewed: CONFIRMED VERIFIED, no defect found.

entries.he: (דף יב:) דכתיב גבי יום הכפורים וכפר הכהן אשר ימשח אותו
entries.en: Scripture says regarding Yom Kippur: "the kohen who is anointed shall make atonement" - limiting the service to the Kohen Gadol.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'דכתיב גבי יום הכפורים וכפר הכהן אשר ימשח אותו' quotes Leviticus 16:32 ('וכפר הכהן אשר ימשח אתו') accurately rendered as 'the kohen who is anointed shall make atonement.' The added clause 'limiting the service to the Kohen Gadol' correctly states the drasha's point (only the anointed/appointed priest may perform it), consistent with entry 002's claim and the linked Horayot 12b citation.

entries.he: ובגמרא (דף ו.) מפרש למה מפרישין: ללשכת פרהדרין. כך שמה
entries.en: The Gemara (6a) explains why the separation is necessary. "To the Parhedrin chamber" - that was the chamber's name.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'ובגמרא (דף ו.) מפרש למה מפרישין: ללשכת פרהדרין. כך שמה' has two dibburim: (1) a forward cross-reference to Yoma 6a for the reason of the sequestering, and (2) a gloss on 'to the Parhedrin chamber' that this was simply its proper name. Both are rendered accurately and completely.

entries.he: ובגמרא מפרש למה נקראת כן:
entries.en: The Gemara explains why the chamber bore that name.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'ובגמרא מפרש למה נקראת כן' = 'and the Gemara explains why it was so called' - matches the English exactly; this is Rashi flagging that the reason for the chamber's name (Parhedrin) is given later in the sugya.

entries.he: ומתקינין לו. ומזמינין כהן אחר
entries.en: "And they prepare for him" - they designate another kohen to serve as High Priest in his place,
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'ומתקינין לו. ומזמינין כהן אחר' = "'and they prepare for him' - and they summon another kohen..." (sentence continues into entry 007's 'להיות כהן גדול תחתיו'). Reading 006+007 together ('they designate another kohen to serve as High Priest in his place, should some disqualifying event befall the Kohen Gadol...') reproduces the full Hebrew meaning exactly once, with no information lost or duplicated across the pair - the split point simply does not fall exactly on the Vilna print-line boundary, which the corpus's dibbur-hamatchil convention treats as normal, not a defect.

entries.he: להיות כהן גדול תחתיו אם יארע בו
entries.en: should some disqualifying event befall the Kohen Gadol before Yom Kippur.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Continuation of 006: 'להיות כהן גדול תחתיו אם יארע בו [פסול]' = 'to be Kohen Gadol in his stead, should [a disqualification] befall him.' Combined with 006's English ('...to serve as High Priest in his place,') and 008's continuation ('should some disqualifying event...'), the full idea is conveyed once, accurately and completely.

entries.he: פסול קרי או שאר טומאה המעכבין
entries.en: The possible disqualification: a seminal emission (keri) or other impurity that bars entry to the Temple.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'פסול קרי או שאר טומאה המעכבין [מלבוא למקדש]' = 'a disqualification: a seminal emission (keri) or other impurity that prevents [entry to the Temple].' 'Keri' correctly glossed as seminal emission; 'bars entry to the Temple' matches the continuing 'מלבוא למקדש' picked up naturally in this entry's English.

entries.he: מלבוא למקדש: ובעד ביתו. גבי
entries.en: "And for his household" - this phrase about the Yom Kippur atonement appears in Acharei Mot.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'מלבוא למקדש: ובעד ביתו. גבי יוה"כ כתיב באחרי מות' = '...from entering the Temple. "And for his house" - regarding Yom Kippur, [this phrase] is written in [parashat] Acharei Mot.' Acharei Mot (Leviticus 16) is indeed the Yom Kippur parasha containing 'וכפר בעדו ובעד ביתו' (16:6/16:11); the English matches.

entries.he: יוה"כ כתיב באחרי מות: א"כ.
entries.en: "If so" - Rabbi Yehudah requires preparing a backup wife lest the first die before Yom Kippur.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'יוה"כ כתיב באחרי מות: א"כ.' completes the citation from 009 and opens a new bare dibbur 'אם כן' (if so) whose actual explanation ('דחיישת למיתה' - since you fear death) is supplied in the next Vilna line (excluded entry 011, not part of this review batch). The English's gloss ('Rabbi Yehudah requires preparing a backup wife lest the first die before Yom Kippur') correctly supplies the antecedent that 'if so' refers back to - Rabbi Yehuda's stated concern in the Mishnah (gemaraContext linked line yoma-002a-l04) that a backup wife must be designated lest the first die. No factual content is misstated.

entries.he: דחיישת למיתה: אין לדבר סוף.
entries.en: Since he feared death - "there is no end to the matter"

riskSignals.reason: English is 4.89x the Hebrew's character length (possible invention or merged content)

entries.reviewerEvidence: HE is 'דחיישת למיתה: אין לדבר סוף.' (two clauses: the tail of the comment on the PRECEDING entry's dibbur hamatchil 'אם כן', then a new quote 'there is no end to the matter'). Current EN ('the Rabbis object: if we worry about death, the backup wife might also die, and so on without end') imports 'the backup wife might also die' from the NEXT entry's Hebrew ('שמא גם זו תמות', rashi-yoma-002a-012, not in this entry at all) and adds framing ('the Rabbis object') not in this entry's Hebrew. Confirmed against the linked Mishnah (yoma-002a-l04): the quoted phrase is the Sages' reply to Rabbi Yehuda, and this entry's own Hebrew only covers 'since [he] feared death' + the new quote.

entries.he: שמא גם זו תמות: גמ' שריפת
entries.en: Perhaps the second wife too will die - the objection stands. The Gemara now opens. "The burning of the cow" -
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'שמא גם זו תמות: גמ' שריפת' = "'perhaps this one too will die.' GEMARA: [the] burning..." This is Rashi's gloss on the Rabbis' retort ('there is no end to the matter') - explaining that even a replacement wife could die, which is exactly what makes the retort valid; 'the objection stands' is a fair one-clause summary of that logic, not a false claim. 'The Gemara now opens' correctly marks the transition at the printed 'גמ'' heading before Rashi's next lemma ('the burning of the cow') begins. Selected for the batch's deterministic blind-QA sample (positional selection by canonical corpus order among provisionally-VERIFIED entries, not risk-based); independently re-reviewed: CONFIRMED VERIFIED, no defect found.

entries.he: הפרה. פרה אדומה: שעל פני
entries.en: "of the cow" refers to the Parah Adumah (red heifer). "On the face of the Birah" - the chamber's location.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'הפרה. פרה אדומה: שעל פני' - 'the cow' correctly glossed as the red heifer (Parah Adumah); 'on the face of' correctly identified as introducing the chamber's location, matching the Mishnah (Para 3:1)/Gemara text 'ללשכה שעל פני הבירה' quoted in gemaraContext yoma-002a-l08.

entries.he: הבירה. לקמיה מפרש מאי בירה:
entries.en: "The Birah" - the Gemara below explains what this term means.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'הבירה. לקמיה מפרש מאי בירה' = "'the Birah' - below [the Gemara] explains what Birah means." Matches; this correctly forwards to the Gemara's actual definition of bira at gemaraContext line yoma-002a-l24 (Rabba bar bar Chana/Reish Lakish dispute), which the Rashi later in this daf (043) draws on.

entries.he: צפונה מזרחה. במקצוע מזרחית
entries.en: "To the north-east" - the chamber was in the northeastern corner of the Temple courtyard.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'צפונה מזרחה. במקצוע מזרחית [צפונית]' = 'northeast - in the northeastern corner' - matches the Gemara's own language at yoma-002a-l08/l20 describing the chamber's location in the Temple courtyard's northeast corner.

entries.he: צפונית של עזרה היתה: שכל מעשיה.
entries.en: "All its rites" of the Parah Adumah had to be performed with implements not susceptible to impurity.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'צפונית של עזרה היתה: שכל מעשיה' continues the location gloss and opens the next dibbur ('all its rites'), whose content (impervious vessels) is elaborated in the immediately following entries (017-021). The summary clause here ('had to be performed with implements not susceptible to impurity') is a fair short preview of that upcoming elaboration and does not misstate anything.

entries.he: של פרה: כלי גללים.  צפיעי בקר
entries.en: "Vessels of dung" (klei gelalin) - implements made from dried cattle dung, which cannot receive impurity.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'של פרה: כלי גללים. צפיעי בקר' = "'of the cow': 'vessels of dung' - cattle dung [cakes]." 'Klei gelalin' correctly transliterated per the corpus's transliteration convention ('"Vessels of dung" (klei gelalin) - implements made from dried cattle dung' matches the style guide's own worked example almost verbatim).

entries.he: מפרש להו במנחות בפ' ר' ישמעאל
entries.en: These three vessel types are explained in Menachot, in the chapter of Rabbi Yishmael.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'מפרש להו במנחות בפ' ר' ישמעאל' = 'they are explained in Menachot, in the chapter of Rabbi Yishmael' - accurately rendered, including the correct chapter-name citation, which the next entry's '(דף סט:)' [Menachot 69b] cross-reference corroborates.

entries.he: (דף סט:): כלי אדמה. שאין עשויין
entries.en: "Vessels of earth" (klei adamah) - not kiln-fired earthenware,
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew '(דף סט:): כלי אדמה. שאין עשויין' = "(69b): 'vessels of earth' - that are not made..." matches; Menachot 69b is indeed the classic locus for the definitions of these three impervious vessel types.

entries.he: ככלי חרס בכבשן אלא מן האדמה
entries.en: but rather made from the earth itself, not fired like earthenware in a kiln.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Entry 020's own Hebrew is only 'ככלי חרס בכבשן אלא מן האדמה' = 'like a clay vessel in a kiln, but rather from the earth' - it says nothing about soft stone, hewing/carving, or imperviousness to impurity. The phrase 'hewn from natural soft stone' belongs to entry 021's own Hebrew ('כאבן רכה וחוקקין ממנה' - like a soft stone, and they hollow out from it), and 'that does not accept impurity' is not present in either 020 or 021's Hebrew (that concept is already established earlier, e.g. gemaraContext line yoma-002a-l18). Because 020's English already states the 'soft stone / hewn' content, entry 021's English then restates it almost verbatim ('carved from chalk-like soft stone; hollowed-out vessels') and also restates 'not fired clay' (already said in 019/020 as 'not kiln-fired earthenware'), producing genuine duplicate content across the pair rather than the corpus's normal single-statement cross-line flow. Independent second pass (re-derived from Hebrew and Gemara context again, not merely re-checked): CONFIRMED, same conclusion and proposed English.

entries.he: היא שהוא כאבן רכה וחוקקין ממנה
entries.en: That is, [earth] that is like soft stone, from which vessels are hollowed out.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Entry 021's own Hebrew, 'היא שהוא כאבן רכה וחוקקין ממנה', means 'that is, [earth] that is like a soft stone, from which they hollow out [vessels]' - its unique content (soft stone; hollowed/carved) has already been pulled into entry 020's English ('hewn from natural soft stone'), and this entry's closing clause 'not fired clay' duplicates the 'not kiln-fired earthenware' fact already stated in entry 019. The pair 020+021 currently states 'not fired clay' twice and 'soft stone, hewn/carved' twice, which is a real information duplication, not the corpus's normal single-statement dibbur split. Independent second pass (re-derived from Hebrew and Gemara context again, not merely re-checked): CONFIRMED, same conclusion and proposed English.

entries.he: כלים: מאי טעמא. תקינו לה כלים
entries.en: "What is the reason" the Sages required these non-susceptible vessels for the Parah Adumah?
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'כלים: מאי טעמא. תקינו לה כלים [הללו]' quotes the Gemara's question 'What is the reason?' regarding the enactment of these vessels; matches gemaraContext lines yoma-002a-l08 (vessel enactment) and yoma-002a-l14 (tevul yom reasoning) which this entry links to, both of which the combined question addresses.

entries.he: הללו: דטבול יום. לקמן יליף בפרק
entries.en: "Because a tevul yom is valid for the Parah Adumah" - the Gemara derives this below,
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'הללו: דטבול יום. לקמן יליף בפרק' = "'these [vessels]': because of tevul yom. Below, [the Gemara] derives [this] in the chapter..." - matches gemaraContext line yoma-002a-l14's statement that these vessels are impervious specifically because a tevul yom priest is valid for the heifer ritual.

entries.he: טרף בקלפי (דף מג:) והזה הטהור
entries.en: in the chapter "Taraf BaKalpi" (Yoma 43b), from the verse "and the pure one shall sprinkle."
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'טרף בקלפי (דף מג:) והזה הטהור' cites the chapter name 'Taraf BaKalpi' (Yoma's fourth chapter, whose opening Mishnah is about drawing lots from the kalpi/urn) at 43b, and the verse 'and the pure one shall sprinkle' (Numbers 19:19). Both the chapter name and daf citation are historically correct for the sugya deriving tevul yom's validity for the heifer, and match the English exactly. Selected for the batch's deterministic blind-QA sample (positional selection by canonical corpus order among provisionally-VERIFIED entries, not risk-based); independently re-reviewed: CONFIRMED VERIFIED, no defect found.

entries.he: כו': כי היכי דלא ליזלזלו בה.
entries.en: "So that they not treat it lightly" -
entries.reviewerEvidence: Entry 025's own Hebrew is only 'כי היכי דלא ליזלזלו בה' = 'so that they would not come to treat it with contempt' - it does not yet state the reason. The added clause 'since a tevul yom (who immersed but awaits sunset) is valid,' pulls forward the premise from entry 026's own Hebrew ('הואיל וטבול יום כשר בפרה'), which then restates the identical premise a few words later ('people might reason: since even a tevul yom is kosher for the Parah Adumah'). The result states the same fact twice in immediate succession rather than once, which is avoidable duplication (unlike elsewhere on this daf, where a pulled-forward phrase is not also repeated in the following entry). Independent second pass (re-derived from Hebrew and Gemara context again, not merely re-checked): CONFIRMED, same conclusion and proposed English.

entries.he: לומר הואיל וטבול יום כשר בפרה
entries.en: people might reason: since even a tevul yom is kosher for the Parah Adumah,
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'לומר הואיל וטבול יום כשר בפרה' = 'to say: since a tevul yom is fit for the cow['s rites]' - this entry's own English is an accurate rendering of its own Hebrew; the duplication problem identified is attributable to entry 025 pulling this content forward prematurely, not to any defect in 026 itself.

entries.he: אין צריך להיות זריזין בה בשמירת
entries.en: perhaps there is no need to be scrupulous about its purity requirements.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'אין צריך להיות זריזין בה בשמירת [טהרה]' = 'there would be no need to be scrupulous in guarding [its purity]' - matches; continues the hypothetical mistaken reasoning being described.

entries.he: טהרה לכך עשו בה מעלות הרבה
entries.en: Therefore the Sages imposed many rabbinic stringencies of purity upon the Parah Adumah,
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew '[שמירת] טהרה לכך עשו בה מעלות הרבה' = '...purity; therefore they instituted many stringencies regarding it' - 'rabbinic stringencies' is an accurate gloss for 'מעלות' (rabbinically enacted stringencies), matching standard usage.

entries.he: לטהרה וזו אחת מהן: כיון דחטאת
entries.en: and this is one of those stringencies. "Since it is a sin-offering [chatat]" -
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'לטהרה וזו אחת מהן: כיון דחטאת' = '...regarding purity, and this is one of them. Since it is a chatat...' - matches; 'chatat' bracketed alongside 'sin-offering' per the corpus's sacrificial terminology convention.

entries.he: היא. חטאת נקראת שנאמר (במדבר
entries.en: the Parah Adumah is called a chatat, as Scripture says in Numbers 19:
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'היא. חטאת נקראת שנאמר (במדבר [יט])' - matches; correctly identifies Numbers 19 as the source verse calling the red heifer a chatat.

entries.he: יט) למי נדה חטאת היא: וחטאת
entries.en: "It is for purification waters, it is a sin-offering." "And a sin-offering requires the north" -
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'יט) למי נדה חטאת היא: וחטאת' quotes Numbers 19:9 ('וְהָיְתָה...לְמֵי נִדָּה חַטָּאת הִוא') accurately as 'it is for purification waters, it is a sin-offering,' then opens the next dibbur 'and a sin-offering requires the north' (chatat slaughter located north of the altar, per Leviticus law) - matches.

entries.he: טעונה צפון. חטאות הקריבות
entries.en: regular sin-offerings brought on the altar are slaughtered in the northern part of the courtyard.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'טעונה צפון. חטאות הקריבות [במזבח]' = "'requires north' - sin-offerings that are brought [to the altar]..." - matches; correctly frames that this halakha of northward slaughter applies to altar-offered sin-offerings.

entries.he: במזבח נשחטות בצפון ולא שזו טעונה
entries.en: This does not mean the Parah Adumah itself must be slaughtered in the north -
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'במזבח נשחטות בצפון ולא שזו טעונה [צפון]' = '...to the altar, are slaughtered in the north; but this does not mean that this one [the heifer] requires [the] north' - correctly sets up the clarification that the heifer, unlike ordinary sin-offerings, is not literally slaughtered north of the Temple altar.

entries.he: צפון שהרי היא נשחטת בהר המשחה:
entries.en: it was slaughtered on the Mount of Olives, outside the Temple entirely.
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'צפון שהרי היא נשחטת בהר המשחה' = '...north, for it is slaughtered on the Mount of Anointing [Mount of Olives]' - 'Mount of Olives' is the standard identification of 'הר המשחה' in the halakhic literature (the heifer was burned there, per Mishnah Para 3:6, outside the Temple courtyard entirely); the added clarifier is accurate, not invented.

entries.he: וכתיב. בפרה (שם) אל נוכח פני

entries.he: בהן פרישה הרי יש לומר על כל בית
entries.en: there is no separation for them; rather, one could say, for the whole patrilineal
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew (confirmed via Sefaria's continuous printing of the same ד"ה) is "...אינך יכול לומר בהן פרישה, הרי יש לומר על כל בית אב..." - there is NO negation word (no אין/לא) attached to "בהן פרישה" itself. The construction "אינך יכול לומר X, הרי יש לומר Y" is a standard Rashi contrastive pattern meaning 'you cannot [simply/vaguely] say X - rather (הרי), one should say Y [instead]', where X = 'בהן פרישה' (blanket separation applying to them collectively, i.e. the whole mishmeret at once) and Y = the correct, refined answer (separation house-by-house, each before its own day). The packet's English inserts a fabricated negation ('there is NO separation for them') and mistranslates the contrastive הרי as causal 'since', which inverts the logic: it reads as 'you can't say there's no separation, because in fact there's a way' (roughly right conclusion, wrong reasoning chain) instead of the actual point, 'you can't [vaguely] say blanket separation applies to them - rather, the correct account is per-house separation.' This inversion is corroborated by the Gemara's own Steinsaltz English (yoma-002b-l12 in gemaraContext), which frames the answer as affirmatively proposing a specific workable mechanism ('There are certainly ways to do so... We could require sequestering for the entire patrilineal family...'), not as negating separation. Independent second pass (re-derived from Hebrew and Gemara context again, not merely re-checked): CONFIRMED, same conclusion and proposed English.

entries.he: לענין

entries.reviewerEvidence: The Hebrew here is the single word "לענין" ("regarding"/"for the matter of") - the daf genuinely does cut off mid-sentence at this exact point, both in Rashi and in the parallel Gemara line (yoma-002b-l28, which itself ends '...הני מילי לענין'). I fetched Rashi's actual continuation on 3a from Sefaria to check the appended editorial claim: it begins 'לענין פז"ר קש"ב - פייס לעצמו שאין פייס בפרי החג אצל המשמרות...' The mnemonic פז"ר קש"ב is real and does appear next (פ=פייס/lottery, ז=זמן/time-blessing, ר=רגל/festival status, ק=קרבן/offering, ש=שיר/song, ב=ברכה/blessing - six ways the Eighth Day of Assembly differs from the rest of Sukkot). But the packet's added note mischaracterizes it as being 'for the priestly watches' own lottery divisions' - lottery (פייס) is only the FIRST of six unrelated distinctions the mnemonic covers (time-blessing, festival status, offering, song, and blessing have nothing to do with lottery divisions), and even that first item is about a one-time special lottery for the Eighth Day's own offering, not a general topic of 'the priestly watches' own lottery divisions.' This is invented content (nothing in the 'he' field of this entry supports it) that is also factually inaccurate in its specific claim about what the referenced material covers. Independent second pass (re-derived from Hebrew and Gemara context again, not merely re-checked): CONFIRMED, same conclusion and proposed English.

English 'on Yom Kippur, the one stated here in Acharei Mot,' matches exactly; verified this correctly introduces a Leviticus 16:5 quotation that begins in the very next entry (028), not a Pinchas quotation.

entries.he: ומאת עדת בני ישראל יקח שני שעירי
entries.en: 'and from the congregation of the children of Israel he shall take two he-goats
entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew 'ומאת עדת בני ישראל יקח שני שעירי' is purely the continuation of the Leviticus 16:5 quotation introduced by the PRECEDING entry (027: 'הוא האמור כאן באחרי מות' = 'it is the one stated HERE in Acharei Mot'). Confirmed via Sefaria (Rashi on Yoma 3a line 4, unsegmented): 'איל אחד הוא - שהיה קרבן ציבור ביוה"כ הוא האמור כאן באחרי מות ומאת עדת בני ישראל יקח שני שעירי עזים לחטאת ואיל אחד לעולה הוא האמור בפינחס למוספין:' The clause 'הוא האמור בפינחס למוספין' ('this is the one stated in Pinchas regarding the mussaf offerings') appears only AFTER the full Leviticus 16:5 quotation ends, matching entry 029's own text ('...הוא האמור בפינחס למוספין'). But the given English for entry 028 - "is the same as the one stated in Pinchas: 'and from the congregation of the children of Israel he shall take two he-goats" - prematurely inserts 'is the same as the one stated in Pinchas' BEFORE the quotation even begins, in a fragment of Hebrew that contains no such interpretive clause at all. This wrongly implies the quoted verse itself is FROM Pinchas, when it is actually the continuation of the Acharei Mot (Leviticus 16:5) verse introduced in entry 027. The genuine 'stated in Pinchas' equivalence clause belongs only at the end (correctly present in entry 029), so its duplication/premature insertion in entry 028 is a misattributed, shifted piece of content that does not correspond to entry 028's own Hebrew. Independent second pass (re-derived from Hebrew and Gemara context again, not merely re-checked): CONFIRMED, same conclusion and proposed English.

entries.he: ועשה
entries.en: And make - the daf ends mid-word here; the comment (explaining the phrase 'and make for yourself,' modeled on the two silver trumpets) continues on 3b.

riskSignals.reason: English is 37.75x the Hebrew's character length (possible invention or merged content)

entries.reviewerEvidence: Hebrew is the two-word catchword 'ועשה' ('and [he shall] make'), the last word printed on daf 3a before the page break; the comment ('ועשה לך - כמו עשה לך שתי חצוצרות כסף') continues on 3b. Verified directly via Sefaria (Rashi on Yoma 3b line 2: 'ועשה לך - כמו עשה לך שתי חצוצרות כסף:' = "'and make for yourself' - like 'make for yourself two silver trumpets' [Numbers 10:2]"), and confirmed the Gemara itself resumes on 3b with '"עֲשֵׂה לְךָ" - מִשֶּׁלְּךָ...' immediately after 3a's final line. The added English content ('the daf ends mid-word here; the comment... continues on 3b') is not a literal rendering of the two-word Hebrew fragment, but every factual claim in it (the mid-word page break, the 'make for yourself' phrase being explained, the silver-trumpets comparison, and the continuation onto 3b) is independently verified as accurate. Given the Hebrew truly is an orphaned page-break fragment, this editorial framing is a defensible and factually correct way to represent it rather than a fabrication or wrong meaning.

riskSignals.reason: English is 23.17x the Hebrew's character length (possible invention or merged content)

entries.reviewerEvidence: The Hebrew for this final entry on the daf is only the single word 'ויכסהו' ('and it covered him') - the dibbur hamatchil (lemma) opening a new Rashi comment that is cut off because the daf ends here (the comment's body continues on 4b, outside this packet's scope). The English translation renders the two-word lemma correctly ('And it covered him') but then adds substantial unsourced narration: '- the daf ends mid-word here; the comment (explaining that the cloud covered the mountain, not Moses) continues on 4b.' This is invented content on two counts: (1) factually the daf does NOT end 'mid-word' - ויכסהו is a complete word, only the comment's explanation is missing, so 'ends mid-word' is an inaccurate editorial claim; and (2) the assertion that the (unseen) continuation explains 'that the cloud covered the mountain, not Moses' is a prediction about content not present anywhere in this packet's Hebrew and not verifiable from the daf-4a data at hand - it presents itself as established fact about 4b's text without any source line to support it. This matches the campaign's known INVENTED_TEXT pattern (narrated content with nothing corresponding in the Hebrew). The lemma itself is correctly translated; only the appended editorial narration is fabricated. Independent second pass (re-derived from Hebrew and Gemara context again, not merely re-checked): CONFIRMED, same conclusion and proposed English.
